title: The Complete Guide to Tax Practice Automation
summary: What tax firms can automate today, from research and prep to return review, where a CPA still decides, and how to roll out AI assistants and agents.
body_markdown:
Tax practices are changing as tax practice automation moves to the forefront. Where before research speed was improved by using generative AI, we are now seeing a shift in firms handing whole workflows to AI agents, not just asking questions to a chatbot.


This guide explores how AI automation is reshaping tax workflows, what it takes to hand real work over to AI agents, and how tax professionals and their teams can handle complex tasks while delivering better results for their clients.


## What is tax practice automation?


Tax practice automation, also called tax workflow automation, is using software to do a firm’s repeatable work, such as gathering documents, entering data, preparing and reviewing tax returns, researching, and drafting, so people spend their time on review and advisory work.


It comes in two camps. The first is automation based on AI assistants, which answer questions and draft notice replies or client replies when you ask (TaxGPT’s Research, Writer, Client Intelligence, and Agent Andrew work this way). The second is automation using AI agents, which handle tax workflow automation end to end and return the result ready for your review (Cowork). In both cases, a person still reviews the output before it goes anywhere.


Tax practice management tools typically track the work, including tasks, client portals, and e-signatures. That keeps a firm organized, but the work itself still lands on staff. TaxGPT does the work it handles tax research and replies, and TaxGPT Cowork runs the full workflows.


## Why firms are automating now


Tax firms are being squeezed from two sides. The work keeps getting more complex, and the number of people available to do it isn’t growing to match. New legislation like the OBBBA adds research, planning, and client questions to a calendar that was already pretty full, and hiring alone can’t close that gap. For many firms, automation now decides how much work they can take on during and off tax season.


Most firms are still in the early stages. Plenty have tried an AI tool or two, but few have built one into the way a return moves throughout their office. Three barriers come up the most when it comes to AI adoption. Implementation takes time nobody has in the middle of a busy tax season. New tools have to work with the software the firm already uses on the daily. And the output has to be accurate enough that a reviewer trusts it instead of having to redo it.


The firms moving now are betting that the next busy tax season will be shorter if they prepare today. They don’t have to automate everything at once, though. A good starting point is to look at each stage of a workflow and ask which pieces are ready to hand off.


## What can you automate, stage by stage


### Client documents and intake


This stage is about getting the right documents squared away. Cowork pulls source documents from SafeSend, SmartVault, Canopy, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and SharePoint. A K-1 workflow extracts the K-1 data and drafts a partner decision memo.[Client Intelligence keeps each client’s profile, linked entities, prior-year positions and documents in one place](https://www.taxgpt.com/tax-client-intelligence) , and TaxGPT Vault handles collecting and managing the documents themselves. The CPA confirms with the client on what is missing from the source documents gathered.


### Return preparation and workpapers


TaxGPT Cowork agents handle return preparation from source documents. They prepare Forms 1040, 1065, 1120 (including consolidated), and 1120-S, create partner K-1s, produce Form 4868 extensions from source documents or an estimate, and handle amended returns on Form 1040-X.


An agent works the way a staff member would. It gathers the source documents, extracts the data, opens your tax software, enters the return, and flags items that need a professional decision. Agents work inside Drake, ProConnect, UltraTax, CCH Axcess, and Lacerte, so your tax software stays the system of record and nothing has to be migrated.


You get a draft return with the open items listed. The preparer resolves the items that need judgment, and the CPA reviews the return and every flagged item before anything is filed.

### Return review


[Agent Andrew](https://www.taxgpt.com/agent-andrew) automates up to 90% of the review process for Forms 1040, 1065, 1120 and 1120-S. It sorts its findings into three groups: Red flags for audit risks, Green flags for missed savings, and Cleared flags for anything that has been resolved. Most reviews take 5 to 10 minutes, against 30 to 90 minutes for a manual senior review. The CPA resolves the flags and signs the return.


### Tax research


[TaxGPT Research](https://www.taxgpt.com/ai-tax-research) turns a plain-language question into a citation-backed answer drawn from the Internal Revenue Code, Treasury Regulations, court cases and IRS rulings. Users can upload files (PDF, JPG, PNG, CSV or Excel) alongside the question to help give more context. TaxGPT Matrix compares rules across US states. The CPA weighs the authority and applies it to the client’s facts.


### Client communication and documentation


[TaxGPT Writer](https://www.taxgpt.com/ai-tax-writer) drafts memos,[IRS notice responses](https://www.taxgpt.com/taxgpt-insights/respond-to-irs-notice) , engagement letters, opinion letters and client emails in the firm’s voice. Every output is a first draft. The CPA edits and approves it before anything goes to a client.


### Tax planning and advisory


Cowork’s[planning](https://www.taxgpt.com/blog/tax-planning) workflows include Tax Planning Strategy, Tax Saving Opportunity Scan, Entity Structure Review and the Interactive Tax Projection Model. For R&D, it offers the R&D Tax Credit Analyzer and R&D credit studies for manufacturing clients and for software or SaaS clients. The CPA reviews the findings and makes the recommendations to the client.


### Bookkeeping


Cowork runs bookkeeping inside the client’s accounting software, including monthly close, reconciliation and an audit trail. The CPA’s role is to review the close.
